Lights for a 3D scene

Source: R/lights-3d.R
light_directional.Rd

Lights combine in lights_3d(), which coord_3d() takes as light, with an ambient term. Each face colour is lit by one shading kernel shared by the vector and raster backends and the view_3d() viewer: the Blinn-Phong model (Phong 1975, Blinn 1977) in linear light, with the ambient, diffuse and specular strengths of the face's material_3d(). Lights follow the light objects of MATLAB (light, camlight headlight), rgl (light3d()), plotly (lightposition) and three.js (DirectionalLight, PointLight, HemisphereLight).

Usage

light_directional(
  direction = c(-1, 1, 2),
  space = "camera",
  colour = "white",
  intensity = 0.65
)

light_point(
  position,
  space = "data",
  colour = "white",
  intensity = 1,
  falloff = 2
)

light_head(colour = "white", intensity = 0.65)

light_hemisphere(
  sky = "white",
  ground = "grey30",
  direction = c(0, 0, 1),
  space = "data",
  intensity = 0.35
)

Arguments

direction

Direction from a surface toward the light, or the sky direction of a hemisphere light.

space

"camera" or "data".

colour, sky, ground

Light colours.

intensity

Nonnegative multiplier of the light colour.

position

Position of a point light.

falloff

Nonnegative exponent of the distance falloff.

Value

A light for lights_3d().

Details

light_directional() shines along a fixed direction from infinitely far away. light_point() sits at a position and its contribution falls off as intensity / d^falloff, with d the distance in panel units (the box side is one, stretched by the camera aspect) and at least 0.001; falloff = 2 is the inverse-square law, falloff = 0 a constant. The falloff never depends on the other geometry in the panel. light_head() is a directional light that shines from the eye, like MATLAB's camlight headlight. light_hemisphere() adds an ambient term that blends from ground to sky as the normal turns from -direction to direction (three.js HemisphereLight).

In space = "camera", x points right, y up and z toward the viewer, and positions are relative to the camera target in panel units. In space = "data", directions are in the normalised panel axes and positions in data units.

References

Phong (1975). Illumination for computer generated pictures. Communications of the ACM 18, 311-317. doi:10.1145/360825.360839

Blinn (1977). Models of light reflection for computer synthesized pictures. SIGGRAPH '77, 192-198. doi:10.1145/563858.563893

Examples

lights_3d(light_directional(c(1, 1, 2)), light_point(c(0, 0, 3), falloff = 2))
